review: A feasibility calculation for the task's route (ii), done before a unit is spent building it. Route (ii)'s ingredient is the site-wise maximal-coupling failure rate alpha_3(p), computed here exactly (0.38791 at p=5, 0.42081 at 23/4, 0.43370 at 6, 0.65303 at 21/2), and the disagreement set is dominated by oriented site percolation with that parameter on the three-parent level DAG. Measured q_c is between 0.425 and 0.43 (survival 0.000 at 0.425 over 600 levels and 200 runs, 0.015 at 0.43, 0.367 at 0.45). So route (ii) certifies to p about 5.9 - a gain of 0.6 over attempt a3's one-site averaged Wasserstein 5.26 - and at the located p = 10.5 its ingredient is 0.653, which would need q_c >= 0.65, half again the DAG's actual threshold: the route fails in its own ingredient, not narrowly, and q_c is a property of the DAG rather than of the estimate. Every criterion built on the one-site failure rate sits in [3.76, 5.9]: branching/Dobrushin 3.7564, averaged Wasserstein 5.26, percolation 5.9, against the located 10.5. q_c is measured, not bounded, so this is a feasibility calculation and not a certificate - stated in section 3. Same model family and machine as a3, disclosed.

triage.note: The run demonstrates what it claims and is explicit that it is a feasibility calculation rather than a certificate. Five assertions: alpha_3 computed exactly in rationals over all 6^3 parent configurations and all single-parent changes, its monotonicity along the line, the percolation survival ensembles at six values of q with fixed seed, the crossing bracketed between p = 23/4 and 6, and the ingredient at the located p = 10.5. What it establishes: route (ii) of the task - disagreement percolation - has a ceiling of about p = 5.9, a gain of 0.6 over attempt a3's 5.26, because the oriented site percolation threshold of the three-parent level DAG measures between 0.425 and 0.43 while alpha_3 crosses it there; and at p = 10.5 the ingredient is 0.653, so the route would need a threshold half again the DAG's actual one. That last point is the useful one: the failure is in the route's own ingredient and is a property of the DAG, so no sharpening of the percolation estimate closes it. Every criterion built on the one-site failure rate lies in [3.76, 5.9] against a located 10.5. NOT established, and section 3 says so: q_c is measured, not bounded below, so this certifies nothing by itself - the only easy rigorous lower bound is the branching 1/3, which returns p < 3.7564; the per-site domination uses the crude one-parent bound, which would refine the constant but not the conclusion since even q_c = 0.5 reaches only p = 6.7; and a3's diagnosis that the one-site ingredient cannot see the ferromagnetic alignment stands. Attempt a3 is by the same model family, machine and running worker; disclosed in the first paragraph, and its 5.26 is not re-derived or contested.
